title: Report: Ubisoft teams asked to justify not using generative AI in project pitches - Ubisoft responds
author: imlo2
selftext:
Following the recent Motherbrain announcement, here's another interesting angle on Ubisoft's generative AI strategy.

Chris Kerr of Vertical Slice reported on 25th of November that according to multiple anonymous Ubisoft employees, teams pitching new projects are expected to explain how they would use gen AI to accelerate development, or justify why it is not appropriate for their projects.

Wccftech also covered this same story, and connected it to Ubisoft's broader AI investment.

According to the story, some of the employees used quite colorful language, they described the situation as "*Top-Down Nightmare of AI Psychosis*".

Ubisoft has now responded saying that projects aren't required to use gen AI and that teams should determine where the technology makes sense.

I wonder what the distinction between requiring AI usage, and expecting teams to evaluate AI is. Or is it just a veiled requirement. Especially when it comes to prototyping, faster iteration and smaller development teams, etc.

What do you think about this kind of approach?

**Sources:**

**Original reporting:** Chris Kerr, Vertical Slice (Nov 25)   
[https://www.verticalslice.news/ubisofts-internal-pitching-process-is-becoming-increasingly-ai-pilled/](https://www.verticalslice.news/ubisofts-internal-pitching-process-is-becoming-increasingly-ai-pilled/)

**Wccftech coverage:** Alessio Palumbo (Nov 26)  
[https://wccftech.com/ubisoft-employee-ai-psychosis-yves-guillemot-genai-push/](https://wccftech.com/ubisoft-employee-ai-psychosis-yves-guillemot-genai-push/)

**Ubisoft response:** reported by VGC (Nov 26)   
[https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/ubisoft-denies-requiring-developers-to-use-generative-ai/](https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/ubisoft-denies-requiring-developers-to-use-generative-ai/)

comments.author: Neither_Berry_100
comments.body:
AI is great in moderation. The engineers themselves probably have the best idea of how to use it. But they could have bias due to laziness or wanting to stay employed.

Management is pushing "super speed" with AI everywhere. The only way to go faster and faster is to reduce control until you don't have any. Management does not understand the tradeoffs. They never have. They just demand more. They don't know that it is possible or how to achieve it. But they demand more anyways.

I'm happy with my current limited usage of AI. I am planning to shift more towards vibe coding for a much later project. But even then I will control the heck out of the core bases. Design. Code. Whatever.

replies.author: FriendlyJewThrowaway
replies.body:
If devs can justify why they’re better off not using AI for technical reasons, they shouldn’t have to use it. If they want the project to cost more or have a lower quality final result because clankers and data centers evil, then they should go finance it themselves.

It seems like a fair policy to me, although I don’t know the extent to which Ubisoft’s execs understand the actual arguments. I don’t think companies should feel obliged to reduce their competitiveness, just because some employees have their own fanciful ideas about how the world should be run.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body:
Well, there is not really proof of that you will be less competitive if you use AI. You can throw in more features, but we do not know yet if you can make a quality game cheaper or better.

Many people oppose extreme adaptation of AI to literally just avoid slop.

AI is literally rewarding people who don’t care about the game and they will be the “high performers” on paper. I know a guy who literally just copies jira tickets into the AI and after being proud of how he became a high performer. Basically slop.

And the problem is that these “high performers”, basically, are loading their work on other people: people who need to review it and QA. Now those people will comment on code/on design etc., they take the time to look through it to make sure everything clicks and leave comments etc. The high performer will just tell the AI to address the comments. His total 10-minute time could cost others hours of work, because basically offloading his brain to the AI and the reviewers. 

The execs rewarding the “productivity” the managers rewarding the “productivity”. Expect many times it will lead to a way worse product and people who actually care about the games are punished, because they do not just copy everything into AI.

So this is the other side of the coin, not the ai itself is the problem, but there is a real ai psychosis and disconnect with many companies execs.

replies.author: Far_Composer_5714
replies.body:
I would imagine if you're a programmer you're not concerned about being unemployed because you've moved too fast. 

Companies always have something to work on because the customers always have something to complain about or the team is promising something that they can't be done in the time that they promised. 

Moving faster just means more work. 

If doing more work is easier then that's probably good? It just depends on how much you like your workflow.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: I don't think it's an unreasonable thing to be asked to justify. There might be legitimate reasons you don't want to use it and companies shouldn't be expected to cover the costs of a development cycle where AI can speed up and improve the work yet the dev team chooses not to use it for reasons that are counterproductive to the company's goals.

comments.author: ConcerningThirst
comments.body: If you are in game dev there is not a single role you can even be in where AI isn't heavily used to improve what you're making. A game dev that won't use AI is not only a liability but a burden.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: Good, they should be rooting out all of their anti-AI employees and getting rid of them as they're poison to the production. Not trying to find ways of accelerating and improving your workflow is practically sabotage.

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body:
I think many of these people who are against AI are just too proud of their perceived "craft", and they feel it's threatened. Over the decades I've seen people who seem love UV mapping and such chores, so no wonder if big parts of boring work are wiped away they might feel threatened, and at the same time they're not willing to learn new things.

But as a (tech)artist/programmer I've got a lot of flak for trying to speed up things already long time before AI. Procedural generation was similarly seen as a soulless replacement for "real art". And it was the same for 3D kitbashing, photobashing for concept art, and numerous other things which now are seen as completely normal.

comments.author: Alternative-Suit5541
comments.body:
Aka pocs and idea showcasing?

Perfect use case, just like 3d printing is for demonstration and show casing ( you have and see something real) no one would 3d print a dish washer or whatever..  but to check size, look and feel? Perfect
